diff --git a/inflection/__init__.py b/inflection/__init__.py
index ffac5ce22e60816f18267d742455e4936b6d1c1a..3471e31976d8c025b6a32c7dd8c3eb791839f24c 100644
--- a/inflection/__init__.py
+++ b/inflection/__init__.py
@@ -360,6 +360,10 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
     create a nicer looking title. :func:`titleize` is meant for creating pretty
     output.
 
+    Words written in capitals, such as acronyms, are kept as they are. When
+    the whole string is in capitals, though, there is no telling acronyms
+    from the other words, so every word is capitalized as usual.
+
     Examples::
 
       >>> titleize("man from the boondocks")
@@ -370,13 +374,32 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       'The Man Without A Past'
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")
       'Raiders Of The Lost Ark'
+      >>> titleize("NASA rocket launch")
+      'NASA Rocket Launch'
+      >>> titleize("HTMLTidy")
+      'HTML Tidy'
+      >>> titleize("NASA_ROCKET_LAUNCH")
+      'Nasa Rocket Launch'
 
     """
-    return re.sub(
+    title = re.sub(
         r"\b('?\w)",
         lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
         humanize(underscore(word)).title()
     )
+    if word.isupper():
+        return title
+    # ``title`` has the words of ``word`` in the same order, apart from a
+    # trailing "_id" dropped by humanize(); put back those written in
+    # capitals. Comparing each pair guards against case mappings that
+    # split a word, like 'İ'.lower().
+    title_parts = re.split(r"([^\W_]+)", title)  # words at odd indices
+    original_words = re.findall(r"[^\W_]+", _separate_words(word))
+    for i, original in zip(range(1, len(title_parts), 2), original_words):
+        if (len(original) > 1 and original.isupper() and
+                original.lower() == title_parts[i].lower()):
+            title_parts[i] = original
+    return ''.join(title_parts)
 
 
 def transliterate(string: str) -> str:
@@ -412,11 +435,19 @@ def underscore(word: str) -> str:
         >>> camelize(underscore("IOError"))
         'IoError'
 
+    """
+    return _separate_words(word).lower()
+
+
+def _separate_words(word: str) -> str:
+    """
+    Insert underscores between CamelCase words and replace dashes with
+    underscores, like :func:`underscore` does, but keep the case of the
+    letters.
     """
     word = re.sub(r"([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])", r'\1_\2', word)
     word = re.sub(r"([a-z\d])([A-Z])", r'\1_\2', word)
-    word = word.replace("-", "_")
-    return word.lower()
+    return word.replace("-", "_")
